# Feature Coverage Matrix

HS2-S2T4VJ: `clients/web/src/features/terminal-drawer.test.ts` covers an aborted hung
create, serialized second create, Retry/Close, a created terminal missing from the
dashboard, and a later stream update. `clients/web/src/components/terminal-drawer.test.ts`
covers the failed tab's cause and controls. The real-parent
`clients/web/tests/terminal-drawer-transitions.spec.ts` hangs a create route, verifies
the busy banner clears and the failed tab is actionable, then retries into a live tab.
Wide, medium, narrow, restored-wide, and dark captures document the failure state.

HS2-JRQG1T: failed AI terminal launches retain a bounded recent diagnostic tab,
exit status, and existing terminal scrollback. The manager's retention and expiry
test, broker and in-process HTTP launch tests, and drawer banner render test cover
the core transitions. The real-browser drawer flow is reviewed manually at wide
and phone widths before ticket completion.

HS2-FVWKJC: `crates/hotsheet-ticketing/src/checkouts/link_relink_tests.rs` covers a
`.hotsheet2/store` relink through setup refresh then the server-style open, relinking back,
an explicit extra store that survives, missing, empty and dangling links, idempotent
repeated refreshes, legacy registries with one or several Git sources, untouched explicit
source sets, a selected-store open first after a relink that keeps the extra store,
and six concurrent opens. The gated live
`clients/web/src/migration-server-integration.test.ts` reopens a relinked migrated project.

HS2-7VB81E: `clients/web/tests/providers.spec.ts` covers explicit Git ticket-repository
linking, rejection of a non-store folder, and both canceling and confirming a
Create collision. `clients/web/src/project-bridge.test.ts` verifies read-only
discovery and no bootstrap when the folder is missing or already holds a store.
The opt-in checkout server integration verifies that discovery leaves the checkout
and Git configuration untouched, then links the store through the real server.

HS2-RJRRSF: `clients/web/tests/terminal-clipboard.spec.ts` selects text with a mouse in a
remote project tab, copies via the keyboard and the right-click menu, checks the viewing
browser's clipboard with the async API unavailable, and verifies shell Ctrl-C with no selection.

HS2-J58Z4Y: `crates/hotsheet-cli/tests/cli.rs # hs2_j58z4y_linked_providers_use_the_nearest_checkout_and_its_default`
checks a two-project machine registry, one mixed Git and external checkout and one
external-only checkout. It verifies per-checkout defaults, a nested working directory,
and explicit refusal when no registered checkout contains the working directory.

HS2-N1QDZW: `hotsheet-jobs/src/watch.rs` unit tests run the shared file watcher
against the real platform backend: four paths registered with one start, repeated
and interleaved writes reported for each path, a path added later, a shallow and
a deep path in one watcher, a directory created after the start, a missing path
refused, a watcher with no path that is filled later, and a dropped watcher that
goes quiet and is started again. `src/signal.rs` unit tests cover the waiter's
wake flag without a watcher: a change between waits, several events as one wake,
a change during a wait, a waiter that cannot watch sleeping out its timeout, and
which events count as a change. `tests/waiter.rs` covers `ChangeWaiter` over
several directories with one platform start, a waiter dropped and started again,
a follower that keeps one waiter across its steps, a kept waiter replaced when
its directory is removed and created again or another checkout is asked for, two
threads waiting through one kept waiter, and the source policy that keeps direct
watcher calls out of `hotsheet-jobs` and `hotsheet-cli`. The coordination wait
and worker view suites cover the migrated callers through the built CLI. Only
macOS was measured; see
[file-watcher-start-cost-2026-11-12.md](file-watcher-start-cost-2026-11-12.md).

Windows Platforms fixes from run 44690376755: `hotsheet-cli/src/process_liveness.rs`
unit tests pin the shared process probe (this process alive, an exited child dead, a
running child alive until stopped, out-of-range pids; HS2-W7E2MJ), and the
`checkout_remove` suites cover its callers. `src/broken_pipe.rs` pins the Windows
closed-pipe codes 232 and 109 (HS2-14GCGH) beside `tests/broken_pipe.rs`.
`hotsheet-jobs/tests/waiter.rs` keeps one waiter on Windows through its directory
identity (HS2-H6E3RB). `hotsheet-server/tests/json_body_policy.rs` rejects
`format!`-built JSON with a displayed path (HS2-CSXZ7K).
`hotsheet-ticketing/src/slash_path.rs` pins the `/` display form of store-relative
paths on both platforms (HS2-T6YXN0). Windows evidence comes from the `Platforms`
workflow; an ARM64 VM run supports it.

HS2-F6F42W: `hotsheet-jobs/src/watch.rs # hs2_f6f42w_*` covers the shared
`BackgroundWatcher`: a start the platform holds up holds up neither its owner nor
its drop, a refused start reported and retried with a backoff that never
shortens until it goes live and reports events, and a path added to a live
watcher going live in the background with both paths reporting. `tests/waiter.rs`

starts through the shared watcher. The callers (coordination wait, worker view,
Codex rollout and Claude transcript followers, the orchestration-settings and
target-store watches) keep their own suites, proved under load for the named
flakes (`hs2_76vmyg`, `hs2_anqxq4`, `hs2_cyhawb`, `hs2_jw6n67`).

HS2-3R9V0R: `hotsheet-jobs/src/github.rs` unit tests cover the gate decision for
every run status and conclusion, covering by a newer run, runs from before the
commit, a diverged branch, a spent lookup budget, the re-watch floor and a
re-run, target validation and its external reference, timestamp parsing, and
cleaning of provider text. `tests/github.rs` drives the source through the real
monitor and store with a scripted `GithubApi`: queued to green with steps, ETA,
URL, and 304 answers that write nothing; red, repeated ensure, and re-watch to
green; a run cancelled for a newer push; cancelled and superseded gates; a commit
the provider does not know yet, and one it never learns, which ends with gate
`unknown` at the HS2-XGV2J9 bound on the injected clock; cancel permitted, refused, undeclared, and never
sent for another commit's run; an unreachable provider, a rate limit with a
requested delay, a malformed body, and a missing repository; hostile provider
text; eight concurrent callers of `ensure_ci_watch`; a lost watch; and
`wait_for_gate_change`. `hotsheet-cli` unit tests cover the API root rule, retry
delays from headers, and remote URL parsing. `hotsheet-cli/tests/job_ci_watch.rs`
runs the built CLI and its real HTTP client against a loopback fixture server
with a synthetic token: `job watch ci` to a green gate, `job watch gate
--wait-seconds`, idempotent repeats, the credential and media type on every
request, no token in any machine-local file, and refused targets. No test
contacts GitHub; a live check against the internal testing repositories was not
run.

HS2-5TC1GQ: `hotsheet-jobs/tests/monitor.rs` steps the watch monitor against the
real store with a manual clock and a scripted source: attach, kinds it does not
serve, lease renewal between polls, steps that write nothing, backoff on
unchanged and failed polls, a vanished operation, outcomes in two checkouts with

release and immediate resume across stop and start, and the read commands. The
process tests passed 20 consecutive runs with retries disabled. Fixtures use

HS2-GCHX8V: `hotsheet-jobs` unit tests compare the transition function with the

Job and checks one gap-free feed sequence. There is no end-to-end surface yet: the

HS2-3FQNGT adds a narrow jsdom `dom-pilot` project for parent-composed search-help insertion and Workers Started/Completed/Started transitions, plus custom-element, shadow-DOM, focus, mutation, composed-event, and re-edit probes. HS2-4B0KSD: `hotsheet-server/src/remote_auth.rs` tests the session lifetime with explicit time:

HS2-PPHJMZ / HS2-JJKVJJ (remote terminals): `hotsheet-server/tests/remote_terminals.rs`
runs a real off-box listener, in process and through the detached broker: a read-only
session lists but cannot open or attach, a read-write session needs CSRF for both,
input echoes through the attached PTY, and revoking the session ends the live stream
and refuses a reattach. HS2-3EDFG2 adds the size arbiter's transitions there: a
driver's normal exit, a revoked driver, a repeated attach and revoke, and a revoked last
viewer each release the claim, so the size recomputes for the remaining viewer and a
later attach sees an undriven size. HS2-CCNRVW adds a reconnect under the same viewer id:
a late normal close and a late revocation of the old connection leave the new connection
driving, and the owner's own close still releases it; `SizeArbiter` unit tests in
`hotsheet-terminals/src/sizing.rs` cover owner release, plain claims, removal and expiry
ending ownership. HS2-AYVQ9Q adds ordered application of size decisions: `terminal.rs` tests
stall an older decision between deciding and applying it (a test-only per-thread hook) and
assert that it never lands after a newer one. Six threads then send repeated claims with
interleaved, out-of-order clocks and stalls, followed by an empty-then-refill pass, and must
settle with the last size frame, the PTY's real grid, and the arbiter's applied size equal. A
`sizing.rs` transition test runs every order of a Workspace Grid zoom, unzoom, zoom against
another device (a late release, the other device's tap, the remounted tile, heartbeats) over
repeated cycles. In each, the newest zoom drives 80×24 after the focus-hold, and the applied
size names it as `driven_by` and `answered_by` even when it took over at the same grid
(HS2-G1ADYV). HS2-G1ADYV's `sizing.rs` tests walk same-size handoffs back and forth with
heartbeats, a passive reconnect, and the old driver leaving (each announced once), a
sub-min-delta handoff, a real resize, and a hold; a `terminal.rs` test asserts that a same-size
focus-hold takeover reaches viewers as one notice frame from the trailing re-decide without a
PTY resize. `clients/web/src/remote-projects/terminals.test.ts` covers the
launch-directory translation and per-server ownership (most specific checkout, legacy
composite launches, no lone-tab claim of a stray terminal);
`remote-projects/transport.test.ts` drives the bridge against two synthetic servers:
each tab attaches with its own session, a reconnect re-resolves, removing one binding
closes only its terminal streams, a revoked registry entry is refused before any
upgrade, a launch reaches the server with the checkout root, another tab's id is
refused, and two checkouts on one server and equal checkout ids on two servers list
disjoint terminals. `clients/web/tests/remote-drawer-create.spec.ts` opens two
read-write remote tabs through the shipped drawer and checks native launch cwd,
live terminal output, tab selection, and isolation (HS2-72HT9Y). Read-only
remote approval and attach remain HS2-NHB2XF.
No customer content was copied into fixtures.

HS2-HSFVHC (remote project prompt parity):
`clients/web/src/remote-project-parity.test.ts` (binaries Vitest project, always on)

permission ownership projection. `clients/web/tests/remote-question-prompt.spec.ts`

against the real server and asserts the hook's answer.

and verifies that the second remote tab sees none of its sessions

HS2-QCBEQF covers the read-only CI batch-gate helper: `scripts/ci-gate.test.mjs`

HS2-M6WXE3 covers immediate context-menu reopening after Escape. The

HS2-R49G01 covers exit-then-reopen AI terminal registration. The terminal manager and

HS2-TQ88K4 covers Kerf Button adoption for standalone actions in the web client. Component unit

This is the durable report for Hot Sheet 2's **double coverage** goal: every shipped
feature should have both focused unit/logic coverage and a realistic E2E user-flow test.
Line/branch reports remain useful floors, but they cannot prove this behavioral pairing.

`clients/web/tests/ux-demo.spec.ts`. Floating-toolbar dark-surface behavior is checked
by the app-shell, terminal-dashboard, and attachment-gallery render tests and by
`clients/web/tests/providers.spec.ts`, `clients/web/tests/gallery-theme.spec.ts`, and
`clients/web/tests/ux-demo.spec.ts` at representative widths.

Update this matrix in the same change that ships, changes, defers, or adds automated
coverage for a feature. Evidence entries are semicolon-separated repository paths; an
optional `# test_name` suffix documents the most relevant test. Manual evidence may use a
Hot Sheet ticket slug when its artifacts are attached outside the repository.
`scripts/check-test-coverage.mjs` validates the rows and evidence references in CI.

Status meanings:

- `double-covered`: both unit and E2E evidence exist.
- `unit-only` / `e2e-only`: one automated layer is missing; this is visible debt.
- `manual`: automation is not currently practical and the manual plan covers it.
- `planned`: the product surface itself is not shipped yet.

HS2-QBMVFQ extends the `web-terminal-drawer` coverage below: the inverse-scale calculation is
covered in `clients/web/src/terminal-viewport.test.ts`, and the Mobile Safari Playwright flow in
`clients/web/tests/terminal-feedback.spec.ts` asserts the scaled xterm viewport and scrollbar stay
on the visible right edge and captures the resulting scrolled terminal.

An active marked description also matches feedback-note warning fill, border, and insets in both inspector and reader, with the standard icon/header in reader mode. A marked description opens the exchange until a regular note answers it, while neutral notes do not; reader mode gives description prompts the same Markdown choices, inline replies, optional general response, and dismissal flow as note prompts. For note-driven feedback, the latest regular-or-feedback note wins: a regular response clears the state and makes the answered ask use ordinary-note presentation, neutral note kinds do not, and a later ask reopens it. Detection for an omitted note kind accepts the case-sensitive `FEEDBACK NEEDED` phrase only at the start of a line (HS2-RG6Z9H: the details rule plus HS1's `IMMEDIATE` prefix, colon optional) and ignores it inside Markdown blockquote lines so a reply that quotes the request back is not mistaken for a new request and does not reopen the exchange (HS2-HG7FZ0), then normalizes note markers to the typed kind and carries the computed state through both compact indexed rows and full-ticket wire responses, preserving response controls when a selected row is replaced by full data. | corruption-resilience                 | docs/02-ticket-storage.md                                                 | A single unparseable ticket file never blocks store enumeration or project open: resilient enumeration and index reconcile/rebuild skip the bad file, still load every healthy ticket, and surface a selectable diagnostic through the shared TicketRow shell. The checkout corrupt-ticket listing parses on the blocking pool so it never stalls other requests (HS2-QV8B7R), and it is served from a per-store stat-validated cache prewarmed at hosting that re-parses only changed files, tracking corrupt, repaired, deleted, and re-corrupted files exactly (HS2-KYSBT2). Newer formats are classified as upgrade-required rather than corrupt and are never auto-downgraded. | terminal-sizing                       | docs/06-clients.md                                                        | Multi-viewer sizing arbitration (focus-follows + smallest/largest/pinned, focus-hold/min-delta/min-interval guards, disconnect self-heal). The focus-follows recency tiebreak advances only on a genuine interaction (`interacting` claim: tap/focus/keystroke), not on the steady heartbeat/geometry claims, so one device's background heartbeats can't ping-pong control and thrash the PTY size — fixing empty/mismatched terminals on a second device such as a phone (HS2-3ZBQDG). A change inside the min-interval is deferred and applied when the window ends, so browsers send one geometry claim per frame with no delayed re-settle (HS2-GSRZX6); a focus-hold takeover likewise re-decides when the hold ends instead of waiting for the next claim (HS2-G4C082); a deferred interaction never suppresses the settled geometry claim, and a closed viewport socket reconnects immediately on typing, pointer, focus, visibility, pageshow, or online instead of waiting out its backoff (HS2-KRQRWH); an OPEN socket that stops answering liveness probes is abandoned and re-attached, and probes never reach the PTY (HS2-51HQ3S) A focused resume of an adopted live viewport sends an interaction claim even if no new focusin arrives (HS2-Y35W56). Only DOM user events (pointer, focus, keydown, paste, input, key bar, paste action) are interactions; xterm's automatic replies to program queries and replayed buffered input are not, a gesture-opened viewport's first eligible claim is interacting, and the arbiter treats first claims, reconnects, and eligibility gains as passive, breaks ties by current driver then attach order, and remembers a departed authority's interaction so it regains the size on reconnect (HS2-1YX5VS). | web-project-live-refresh              | docs/04-core-server-cli.md; docs/06-clients.md                            | Selected-project ticket changes from external CLI/git writes silently refresh healthy rows and merge unrelated inspector fields through a cursor-replay-safe WebSocket-first stream without flashing foreground loading UI. The credential-free browser bridge keeps loopback secrets server-side; one poll handshake plus one subscribe-race replay precede idle push with zero recurring requests. Disconnects, unsupported upgrades, and older non-replayable server frames replay through the genuine blocking long poll, reconcile once, and retry WebSocket with capped exponential backoff; overflow uses the same authoritative recovery. Any open metadata select defers and coalesces refresh until its popup closes, including the new-ticket composer while a background ticket moves columns; an active draft adopts remote-only changes, preserves local-only/converged edits, ignores this client's own in-flight partial autosave, and surfaces only genuine same-field divergence in a side-by-side editable merge; stale whole-ticket tokens retry unrelated field updates against the fresh token. A just-created ticket is retained across every background refresh until an eventually-consistent index actually contains it, so a stream-triggered refresh whose fetched page has not yet indexed the new ticket cannot drop the optimistic row or deselect it — it reappears authoritatively once indexed, without duplication, and stops being retained after a TTL (HS2-Y5PDHW; manual end-to-end check in docs/manual-test-plan.md). While a workspace search is active a background refresh keeps the visible search results and does not filter the selection against the base-view page, so a matching ticket that is not on the first base page stays selected (HS2-6AXG6Z). | board-column-pagination               | docs/06-clients.md                                                        | The column (board) view paginates per column: each status column (Not Started/Started/Completed/Verified) loads more with its own status-filtered query and cursor, so a long column never starves a short one and every column with fewer loaded rows than its absolute lifecycle total shows its own Load more control — instead of a single global cursor whose one continuation landed in an arbitrary column. Loaded rows stay in one flat union (selection/inspector/mutation/drag unaffected); a background refresh restores each user-expanded column to its loaded length in a single commit so an external change never resets a column's pagination to the baseline; single-collection views (Backlog/Archive/Trash) and search keep the global cursor (HS2-8NBGBX). A column pages an ordered list of statuses in turn, not just one: when the Hide Verified column setting merges Verified into Completed, that column exhausts its `completed` stream then continues into `verified` (per-status cursors tracked in the column page), so verified rows beyond the initial global page stay reachable through its own Load more and the column reaches its full done total; the background-refresh restore re-fetches each merged status stream independently (HS2-F2N4ZN). The board's initial load is per column too: each status column reads its own first 100 rows in the active sort (one counted request, the rest `counts=false`), so a short column shows every ticket at once and never a lone Load more; refreshes reload expanded columns in pages of at most 500 and warm tabs keep column cursors (HS2-HNZZHC) | path-canonical-spelling | docs/04-core-server-cli.md | Every canonicalization under `crates/` goes through `hotsheet_sync::paths::canonicalize`, which drops the Windows verbatim prefix (`\\?\C:\`, `\\?\UNC\`) whenever the ordinary spelling names the same file (under `MAX_PATH`, no device name, trailing dot or space, or forbidden character), so Git arguments, printed commands, registered checkout roots, store locators and checkout ids use one ordinary spelling; Git's own `C:/...` output is read back in native form. ## Coverage report layers

### Selected disabled transfer admission (HS2-DJWTB0)

The server test
`routes::providers::disabled_transfer_tests::hs2_djwtb0_owned_authenticated_transfer_admission`
launches one explicitly isolated ignored child. Four named called scenario sources
cover initial both-position policy and missing-peer-credential precedence across
GitHub/Jira/GitLab/Git metadata; copy/retry/disable/re-enable/move provenance;
effective routing, defaults, same ID and missing IDs; and bounded registration-descriptor
rendezvous for final-check toggle plus external-to-Git reclassification. The last scenario
is called with two transition variants. These are one discoverable parent and one ignored
child entrypoint, not six independently executed tests.

The fixture owns real Git ticket stores and synthetic credentials only after compiled
capability checks. Exact disabled 409 responses, provider ticket-method counters and
unchanged bytes/counts support the intended refusal. Native credential reads are not
instrumented: missing-peer-credential precedence is an additional behavioral control,
not a measured secret-get count. No UI or manual/live-provider validation is claimed.

- Rust line coverage: `cargo llvm-cov`; CI uploads `rust-coverage-lcov` and enforces
  the current line floor.
- Migrator line/branch/function coverage: `npm run test:coverage` in `migrator/`; CI
  uploads `migrator-coverage-lcov` and enforces Vitest thresholds. Since Vitest 4
  (HS2-XKYSVK) its AST-aware v8 remapping reports the same suite lower: `export.mjs`
  75.9% lines, 68.2% branches and 70.0% functions, so the function floor has no headroom.
- Feature double coverage: this matrix, gated by `npm run`-free
  `node scripts/check-test-coverage.mjs` in CI.
- Manual-only behavior: [manual-test-plan.md](manual-test-plan.md).

The matrix reports whether both behavioral layers exist; it does not claim every
requirement is fully asserted merely because a file is listed. Reviews should still
inspect the named tests and add transition/adversarial cases for stateful changes.
For stateful clients, double coverage specifically requires both synchronization
directions (control → state/output and programmatic state → live control properties),
all visible actions, reset/replacement round trips, and a post-reset edit. Merely
rendering or touching a control does not satisfy the behavioral layer.

The LAN-origin WebKit identity scenario separately records the exact native, stackless
`ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.` diagnostic. WebKit
[documents this as next-frame observation deferral](https://webkit.org/blog/9997/resizeobserver-in-webkit/).
The diagnostic count must stop increasing across three final rendering frames; all other
page errors, including application exceptions with that message, fail the test. Functional
identity and real-store persistence assertions still run in full.

### Native Claude terminal turn usage (HS2-W2GNTT)

`HS2-TTYZGX` adds unit coverage for Anthropic's published Fable 5.1 ordinary input/output and separate cache-read, five-minute write, and one-hour write prices. The transcript parser prices deduplicated message records while preserving total input tokens for display; unclassified cache writes remain unpriced rather than assigned a guessed TTL. The terminal HTTP test and timeline browser test cover the recorded and rendered cost.

- Behavior: matcher-free Claude prompt and stop hooks run in a live terminal; the first boundary starts a transcript follow (offset zero before file creation) and a prompt snapshots the unique live ticket claim. Each assistant message is recorded once it is final (HS2-SSMDQ1); Stop or failure waits briefly for a delayed append and records the last one, once per message id. Duplicate stops, old transcript rows, changed sessions, ambiguous claims, and claims acquired after the prompt cannot misattribute a turn.
- Unit: `crates/hotsheet-aitools/src/claude_transcript_usage.rs` covers repeated and out-of-order assistant rows, cache tokens, malformed and subagent rows, empty then refilled files, mixed models, and truncation; `crates/hotsheet-server/src/routes/terminals/claude_usage.rs` checks transcript path binding.
- End to end: `crates/hotsheet-cli/tests/cli.rs # permission_hook_reports_claude_turn_boundaries_without_prompt_content` checks hook payload privacy against a TCP server; `crates/hotsheet-server/tests/http.rs # native_claude_turn_usage_is_deduplicated_and_bound_to_its_start_claim` checks the authenticated route, claims, raw events, and repeated boundaries through the real server router.

The real `GET /checkouts/{checkout}/tickets/{ticket}/usage` response returned both for the test ticket; `HS2-W2GNTT` carries the evidence. Fable 5.1 was unpriced during that run; `HS2-TTYZGX` adds its published rates for new events.

### Ticket-store attachment compaction (HS2-T2Q7KM)

- Behavior: a dedicated, clean Git ticket store previews only duplicate or oversized attachments on old completed, verified, or archived tickets; the fingerprint binds the plan to its branch head. Execution needs an exact confirmation, a new external mirror backup, `git-filter-repo`, a single branch with no tags, and a matching remote-head lease. A disposable clone records tombstone notes before selected attachment paths leave history; the original checkout remains stale and untouched.
- Unit and real Git flow: `crates/hotsheet-ticketing/src/repository_compaction.rs` covers eligibility, duplicate/oversize reasons, dirty and embedded-store rejection, confirmation, disposable-clone rewrite, mirror backup, preserved original, and leased bare-remote push. CI installs a pinned `git-filter-repo` for the rewrite test.
- Large-plan path safety (HS2-M0VTRA): the same module tests a 20,000-candidate paths file larger than the process argument limit through `git-filter-repo --dry-run`, plus a real disposable-clone rewrite of filenames containing a line break and the `==>` directive marker. The temporary path list is removed after execution.
- Historical orphans (HS2-JRT1ZP): the same module inventories deleted attachment paths with bounded Git history records and blob identities, including multiple versions and unusual filenames; excludes current and unrelated paths; records blob/deletion provenance in a retained manifest; and verifies the disposable rewrite against a bare remote and mirror backup. The CLI compaction integration test checks orphan details in the JSON preview, the web RepositorySize unit test checks the orphan preview row, and the shipped project-statistics browser test checks that row at wide, medium, narrow, and restored-wide sizes.
- Execution and recovery (HS2-RFJ1GN): the core test proves the private recovery marker blocks stale writes and sync after the remote rewrite, refuses premature clearing, and permits a clean checkout restored to the exact origin head. The authenticated server HTTP test covers denied execution, exact confirmation, mirror backup, force-push result, and a guarded original checkout. The shipped browser flow covers exact confirmation, server refusal, success result, and recovery guidance after wide, medium, phone, and restored-wide preview checks. The CLI `--recover` verifies the restored checkout before clearing its guard.
- Manual: `docs/manual-test-plan.md # Multi-collaborator attachment compaction recovery` covers two separately held checkouts against one disposable shared remote.
- End to end: `crates/hotsheet-cli/tests/cli.rs # checkout_compact_previews_and_requires_exact_execution_confirmation` checks the headless plan and consent path; `crates/hotsheet-server/tests/http.rs # repository_compaction_previews_only_old_closed_git_attachments` checks authenticated preview and execution; `clients/web/tests/providers.spec.ts # project statistics previews and executes ticket-store compaction` checks the shipped composition and execution states; `clients/web/tests/ux-demo.spec.ts # RepositorySize demo exposes compaction preview, loading, and unavailable states` checks catalog variants at wide and narrow widths.

### Existing note as a feedback response (HS2-J4G9GB)

- Behavior: `note_id` plus `response_to` (CLI `--edit-note --response-to` / `--clear-response-to`, MCP `hotsheet_update`, ticket and provider PATCH) links, relinks, or unlinks an existing regular note as the response to an earlier feedback request on the same ticket. No reply is appended. Re-linking the same request writes nothing. An invalid link is a 400 that refuses the whole request before any field changes. A stale `expected_token` is a 409 `ticket_changed`. A human link of AI text sets `human_edited` and keeps the author. Git advertises `note_response_link`; GitHub, Jira and GitLab refuse it explicitly. The note menu's **Link as Feedback Response** and the AI repair preview use the same rule.

### Typed write-behind-unavailable refusal (HS2-DEVEYE)

- Behavior: a queued provider batch on a connection without durable write-behind is refused with 409 and `code: "write_behind_unavailable"`. The single-ticket and batch edit paths fall back to synchronous updates only on that code. Any other 409, including one whose text says "unavailable", stays a refusal, and the `ticket_changed` retry is unchanged.
- Unit: `crates/hotsheet-server/tests/jira_outbox_http.rs # write_behind_unavailable_refusal_carries_a_typed_code_hs2_deveye` and `unrelated_queued_conflict_has_no_write_behind_unavailable_code_hs2_deveye` (route level); `clients/web/src/ticket-field-reconciliation.test.ts # HS2-DEVEYE` (predicate: code required, reworded text accepted, text-only/other-status/other-code refused, disjoint from the concurrency retry).
- End to end: `clients/web/tests/providers.spec.ts # HS2-DEVEYE` edits a write-behind ticket title in the real inspector. The typed refusal takes the synchronous PATCH and updates the row; an unrelated "unavailable" 409 shows its error with no PATCH. The bulk parent (multi-select, then Change priority) covers the same two outcomes. The typed refusal sends one synchronous PATCH per qualified ticket and both rows reconcile. The unrelated 409 sends no fallback write, rolls the optimistic rows back, shows the error, and keeps the selection. In both cases a further action after the outcome queues cleanly. Each pair fails when its own call site reverts to the substring match. The existing queued flow `# HS2-YSF8TV` still passes.
- Manual: none new.

### No Response Needed targets (HS2-VBFSZJ)

- Behavior: `response_to` accepts exactly the notes reads present as feedback requests, including a legacy implicit marker note. Explicit Regular, cross-ticket and nonexistent targets stay 400s, never a `ticket_changed` retry. When a dismissal's request is resolved by another writer while the reader editor is open, the stale-token retry writes nothing, closes the editor, and shows an honest notice instead of an error. This applies to both the workspace reader and the linked reader frame.

One case is the stale reader editor after a correction to Regular: one 409 write and no resend, no stored response, reload, and after captures at wide/medium/narrow/wide. The other dismisses a legacy implicit request from the list inspector's Respond to Feedback, covering a failed write and its retry, a selection change while the write is held, the stored `response_to` link, the request counts and qualified target, and reload. `clients/web/tests/ticket-reader-stack.spec.ts # HS2-VBFSZJ` covers the linked reader frame. Each client and server change was confirmed by a mutation that makes its test fail.

Each observes a real 409 then 400, no stored response, retained reply draft without note-edit merge UI, further editing and reset, then a current-request 200 storing the identical text. ### Coordination pool identity after a checkout or store move (HS2-67N8SJ)

- Behavior: a pool whose `project_id`/`source_id` predate a move is migrated under the pool lock only when the checkout registry proves both ids. The project proof is the relocated durable id or the current id at the shipping root. The source proof is a `sourceAliases` chain from the stored connection id to a linked source at the current store path. A migration keeps every other field and logs one line to `identity-migrations.log`. Every other mismatch is refused, and the error names `coordination repair-identity [--dry-run]`, the headless report-and-migrate path that never force-rebinds. `scripts/push.sh` names the same command and resolves a linked worktree's source store through the shipping checkout's `.hotsheet2/store` link.
- Unit: `crates/hotsheet-cli/src/coordination/identity_tests.rs # hs2_67n8sj_*` covers these cases with isolated registry homes and temp repos: a relocated checkout plus a renamed store migrated automatically; a project match with a foreign source chain refused; an unrelated pool or no registry refused; an alias cycle refused without looping; a source-only move refused, then proven; a dry run that writes nothing; a current pool that is a no-op and an absent pool that is not created; eight concurrent opens migrating once; and repeated repairs that are idempotent. `scripts/main-integration-authority.test.mjs # HS2-67N8SJ` covers the id-mismatch and schema-mismatch error text. `scripts/main-integration-window.test.mjs # HS2-67N8SJ` covers the order of worktree source-store resolution: an explicit store, then the worktree's own link, then the shipping link, then the repo path, with a malformed shipping link refused.
- End to end: `crates/hotsheet-cli/tests/coordination_identity.rs # hs2_67n8sj_*` runs the real CLI: a dry run, a repair, a rerun reporting `current`, and `status` keeping the worker; an unproven pool fails `status`, naming the command, and `repair-identity` exits nonzero without writing.
- Manual: none.

### Interrupted browser runs release the Vite fixture server (HS2-F6F8MA)

- Behavior: Playwright's detached `webServer` group runs Vite through `clients/web/scripts/owned-server.mjs --exit-on-stdin-eof`; when the runner ends by any signal (including `SIGTERM` and `SIGKILL`, which skip Playwright's teardown), the closed stdin pipe stops Vite (`SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` after the grace) and the launcher sweeps its own live group. Ownership is the launcher's child handle and its own group only; no pid, name, or port lookup (docs/12 §12.7.10).
- Unit: `clients/web/scripts/owned-server.test.mjs # HS2-F6F8MA` covers argument parsing, EOF/error/signal stop, single stop, grace force-kill, no signal after reap, exit-code propagation, group sweep only when leading, the opt-in stdin binding, and (`# HS2-DXVH3Q`) a group signal dispatched after the server close it caused still sweeping the group. `clients/web/src/playwright-config.test.ts # HS2-F6F8MA` pins the launcher command.
- End to end: `clients/web/scripts/owned-server.e2e.test.mjs # HS2-F6F8MA` launches real processes the way Playwright does and proves runner `SIGKILL`/`SIGTERM` release the owned port and every owned descendant (same-group straggler, detached stdin-bound descendant), foreign same-command processes survive, `SIGTERM`-ignoring servers are force-killed, and a real Vite tree including esbuild exits; fixtures are identified by pid and start time. `# HS2-XH1S69` covers the file's own leaks: it fails fast when `ps` is unavailable, sweeps every POSIX group it created in `afterEach` (proved by an unrecorded foreign fixture whose `SIGTERM`-ignoring descendant must still exit), and bounds every fixture's lifetime. On Windows those identities come from one warm process-table helper rather than a PowerShell cold start per query (HS2-S5BQRD; `clients/web/scripts/windows-process-table.test.mjs` covers its line protocol, shared queries, restart, and timeout).
- Manual: none; reproduced before and after the fix with an interrupted `npx playwright test` stage (ticket HS2-F6F8MA notes).

### Orchestration throughput scheduler (HS2-ECWG50)

- `scheduler_tests.rs` tables the scoring (priority against each urgency term, the
  capped terms, aging and the provisional risk weight) and walks the packing cases
  the ticket names: aging that ends starvation under a stream of fresh high-priority
  work, a limited tool moving work to another allowed tool and back at its reset,
  tool and account caps across targets, a degraded tool taking one probe, a machine
  below its RAM floor and each other machine limit, targets sharing one machine, a
  refusing target with doubling backoff, a policy change mid-run in every way a
  session can fall outside it, a lowered cap, a session waiting on CI refilled with
  independent work, a red gate's repair outranking equal work, sessions the
  scheduler does not own, idle wind-down with `keep_warm`, and held resources. A grid
  of loads proves no schedule passes a cap. Sequences apply each schedule like an
  executor would: an empty queue that refills without a second session, work that
  comes and goes for an hour without a restart, the cooldown in both directions, and
  the same answer for repeated, reordered and duplicated inputs. The decision
  journal, the placement memory (per owner, never created by a read, damaged or
  newer data left alone) and the session view are checked to hold identifiers only.
- `tests/scheduler.rs` drives the shared runtime against real git stores, a scripted
  capacity probe and the recording executor: nothing scheduled without a policy; a
  dry run that logs and applies nothing; an automatic pass that starts one session
  per step and no more on repeats; an approval filed once and honoured after a
  person answers; a denied approval and a missing grant; the unavailable and the
  failing executor; a refused start and a full machine backing off without another
  read; every standing `explain` can answer; a recorded tool limit moving the next
  start and waking followers; wind-downs through the gate, by policy and under
  approval; a run's pending CI gate freeing its session; and the follower stepping
  on start, run events, the wake marker and a named retry time, and never otherwise.
  `tests/scheduler.rs # hs2_1jfvcj` plans a step while a follower waits and shows it
  is woken by the step's readiness event, never by the wake marker first, so the pass
  that reads the new work is logged as `event` (HS2-1JFVCJ; it failed 3 of 3 before
  the fix).
- `remote_servers/scheduler.rs` uses the owned CLI process with no server running
  (capacity unknown, dry by default, applied with backoff under an automatic
  policy), then a real server behind its bearer: the routes, the loop starting when
  the policy enables it, a readiness event causing the next pass, and the stdio MCP
  tool reading the same schedule and log.
  `remote_servers/scheduler.rs # hs2_pnca93` turns automatic placement on with the
  owned CLI while a server runs, reads the log only through the CLI (a scheduler
  request would start the loop itself), and sees the server's loop start with no
  restart and no server request (HS2-PNCA93; it failed without the wake follower).
- `contracts.spec.ts # HS2-ECWG50` validates the real server's schedule,
  explanation, tick, decision log and policy `placement` responses against the

hs2_awb7bx` follows a remote target through the peer's wait and ends on a peer

  backed off and then replaced; a permission request for a start answered under the
  scheduler's operation id, and a stop that never asks; an idle session wound down only at a safe point (mid
  turn, uncommitted work, then committed), with the idle time restarting after work;
  takeover here and at the host, never wound down and still counted; a crash replaced
  twice over and not replaced once the work is gone; an unreachable host concluding
  nothing; a stale unconfirmed start ended as never started; a policy without a
  placement actor reading no host; and a disabled target's session kept for a person.

  plans new work: the step ends with no pass, launch, session record or log entry, and

  before the fix).

  workspace fake agent: a dry tick starts nothing; enabling automatic placement
  starts one session for the confirmed step in the drawer; the terminal is killed and
  the loop replaces the lost session; the ticket is completed and the session is
  wound down at its safe point at the time the earlier pass named. The test waits

  Windows.

  resource through the real claim service: an unbound namespace reads the machine's
  claim; once the project binds it, the machine's claim of the same name is not the
  project's, the hosted wait is free, a claim taken in the project's backend is held
  and waited on there until released; a project-bound backend that cannot be read
  reports the project configuration's `provisional` policy for that namespace only.
  The scripted sources of `tests/capacity.rs` and `tests/scheduler/resources.rs`
  follow the `project` argument; `remote_servers/resources.rs` still passes.

### Redo of a scheduler session's run (HS2-DBCN9N)

- `tests/provisional.rs # hs2_dbcn9n` places an orchestrator-owned session on the
  reopened run and forgets every `work_start` rule: a remembered `session_start`
  rule lets the redo cancel at once with nothing asked (repeated reconciliation adds
  nothing); without it the card asks `session_start` for `codex` under the `redo-`
  operation, unanswered reconciliations do nothing and repeat the one request,
  Allow Once cancels as the redo (not a person's hold), and a denial falls back to the
  HS2-2K0DM8 ask once. It pinned a defect: the check carried no load, so the policy
  always refused it.

### The integrator on demand (HS2-4JQ41V)

- `integrator_session_tests.rs` (core) walks the integrator states (none, starting,

- `tests/session_executor.rs # hs2_4jq41v` runs the real pass: three integrators whose

### One pool per project (HS2-5P112Z, HS2-B2N8EH)

- `project_role_session_tests.rs # hs2_5p112z` (core) pins the home rule and walks a
  project of two sites. Work named only on the site places the dispatcher on the home
  and the worker on the site. The worker's run keeps the home dispatcher. A handoff in
  the home's pool places the home's integrator, while one in the site's own pool starts
  nothing. Both role sessions wind down once integrated. The suite also covers:
  - an entry naming a site, which starts nothing until the site is separated into its
    own project and nothing again once it is grouped back;
  - an offline, unknown-pool or disabled home, which starts no role anywhere while the
    work still goes to the site;
  - two projects, each with its roles on its own home;
  - the dispatcher taking the home's last slot when another site has room, and not when
    that site is disabled or full;
  - a role session on a non-home site keeping its own target's rule.
- `project_role_session_tests.rs # hs2_70z2z6` (core, HS2-70Z2Z6): the dispatcher's
  room rule counts requirements and caps per site. A one-slot home is left to a
  Linux-only step the site cannot run, also with a worker already on that site; the
  dispatcher takes the last slot when the site can run the step, or starts beside it
  when the home has spare room; and work no site can run starts no dispatcher and
  stays unplaced with `requirement_unmet`. `e2e_sites.rs # hs2_70z2z6` runs the
  peer-outage scenario with Auto role sessions on two real servers.
- `project_role_session_tests.rs # hs2_syzb33` (core, HS2-SYZB33): an entry on a site
  is a `role_sessions_not_home` warning naming the home, never a problem, starts no

  service: `policy role-sessions --target <site>` stores the entry and answers the
  warning on stdout and as a line on stderr; validate and the dry run stay valid with

- `code_ref_watch.rs # hs2_xa9dza` (HS2-XA9DZA) sorts remote-tracking paths from
  local ones, resolves one common directory for a checkout and its worktree, records a

  made before the stream is live by the local re-read once and a local commit never,

  no session, then worked, then released (each push wakes), then given up (a push

- `orchestration-settings-model.test.ts # HS2-SYZB33` pins the site hint and lock;

- `tests/site_pool.rs # hs2_5p112z` runs the hosted `target-pool` route on a real home
  checkout with a bare `origin` and a second clone as the other site. A member joins

- `sites_tests.rs # hs2_3jgpdr` joins a site's connection id to the home's by source

### Dispatching the steps the scheduler places (HS2-YC2P7K)

- `session_tests.rs # hs2_yc2p7k` links a session to a run without a state change,
  idempotently, moves it on a refill, refuses a finished session, and validates the
  hosted origin's ticket.
- `tests/session_executor.rs # hs2_yc2p7k` runs real scheduler passes over the real
  session runtime with the scripted host:
  - a refused session start leaves its run queued and the step in progress, and the
    session after the backoff is linked to that same run, with one run in all;
  - without `work_start` in the policy nothing is dispatched and no session starts;
  - a finished run frees its session, which is given the next step's run (refill,
    `session_assigned`), and a cancelled run is replaced by `sched-run-<step>.2`
    while the finished step never is.
- The `hs2_95swq4` executor tests now also assert:
  - one run per step, and the session linked to it and busy while it is unfinished;
  - the step in progress, with later passes keeping the session `busy`;
  - a crashed session's replacement linked to the same run, with the loss on the
    run's stream;
  - a free session refilled with its step's run, assigned once.
- `remote_servers/session_executor.rs` runs the automatic loop on a real server
  with the run dispatched, the tab labelled with it, a killed session replaced on the
  same run, and the run completed before the wind-down.
- `remote_servers/session_work.rs # hs2_yc2p7k` walks the whole chain on one real
  server with the push-capable fake agent:
  1. an automatic policy and a confirmed step;
  2. the loop dispatches one dispatcher-mode run and starts one session linked to
     it, and the step is in progress with the ticket Up Next;
  3. the session's launch shows the checkout, its instructions, its MCP config, its
     worker id and its role;
  4. the role prompt is delivered when the tool comes up and asks for the exact
     ticket;
  5. the session joins the pool;
  6. a claim under its worker id through the server makes the run `dispatched` to
     that worker from the change feed alone;
  7. completing and releasing the ticket completes the run and finishes the step;
  8. the session is wound down at its safe point after its idle time, with one
     session and one run in all.

  The test plays the agent's part: it registers in the pool and claims and finishes
  the ticket through the server's routes, as the skill would.

- Not verified: a real tool's skill doing those steps (manual plan); a target on a
  second server; a target pool with a live dispatcher choosing the session.

### Scheduling around claimable resources (HS2-2FG91X)

- `resource_tests.rs` tables the names against the claim service's rules and every
  reading of one resource: free, held, lapsed, held on another machine, another
  resource of the namespace, unreadable under each offline policy and under both,
  held and unreadable, and a target that was not read. Each case is checked for the
  reason, the contention entry, the same answer for reordered inputs and its wire
  form. Sequences walk one resource through two ready steps: one given it, the
  other deferred, the holder's claim read, a renewal moving the retry time, an early
  release, a new holder, the last millisecond before the expiry and the expiry
  itself, an empty pass and a refill. Further cases cover two claims of one
  resource, two targets on two machines and on one, several resources per step, a
  free session taking the work and its resource, the per-step standings, the
  policy's `placement.resources` problems and the snapshot's `claims_offline`.
  `readiness_tests.rs # hs2_2fg91x` covers a step's declaration: stored sorted,
  unchanged for the same set in another order, a new revision for a changed one,
  withdrawn by a definition without it, ignored by readiness, and refused without
  a write when invalid.
- `tests/scheduler/resources.rs` drives the shared runtime with the recording
  executor on the real local claim backend: two ready tickets needing one VM, where
  one session starts and is told what to hold, the scheduler claims nothing, the
  other is deferred with the claim's expiry, a renewal moves it, and a release
  starts it; a following loop that reads nothing while the VM is held and is woken
  by the claim service's release signal alone; a target on another machine whose
  claim is read from that machine over the reviewed transport while the same name
  held locally changes nothing; the policy's per-target requirement; validation at
  both declarations and agreement of the names with the claim service's parsers; a
  ninth namespace read as unknown; and the local backend failing closed on damaged
  state without rewriting it. A scripted claim source covers what the local backend
  cannot: an expiry and a renewal at chosen times as named retry times, and an
  unreachable backend under `fail_closed` (deferred, backed off, not read again,
  placed once it answers) and under `provisional` (one unverified start, the next
  deferred, reconciled when the backend returns).
- `remote_servers/resources.rs` uses the owned CLI process with no server
  (`--resource`, the policy file, the claim CLI taking and releasing the VM, `plan`,
  `explain` and the decision log), then a real server: the routes validating the
  declaration, the loop deferring the work, and a release through the claim route
  causing a `signal` pass with nothing else happening; and the stdio MCP tools
  declaring a requirement, acquiring the resource and reading contention.
- HS2-G1PKK2: `tests/scheduler/resources.rs` follows a VM held on a peer through the
  peer's own wait over the transport fake: a release, a lapse with the test clock
  never reaching the expiry, and a renewal past the old expiry with no wake until the
  release each give one `signal` pass; an unreachable peer ends the watch after one
  failed request with no wake; a direct follow ends on a passed deadline, a gate
  refusal and a peer that cannot wait, and writes the wake marker when free; the
  hosted route answers from this machine's backend and validates its query.
  `remote_servers/resources.rs # hs2_g1pkk2` parks a full-length hosted wait on a
  live service until a release through the claim route answers it.
- `contracts.spec.ts # HS2-2FG91X` validates the real server's plan step, ready
  list, policy, capacity snapshot, schedule, explanation and decision log with the
  new members against the contract.
- HS2-7YSKXE: `tests/session_executor.rs # hs2_7yskxe` places work that needs a VM,
  checks the started session's prompt names it and tells it to acquire it itself, that

- HS2-KCEHVR: `tests/scheduler/resources.rs # hs2_kcehvr` binds two namespaces to

### Orchestration prerequisites and readiness (HS2-42TARA)

- `readiness_tests.rs` tables every gate state against each ticket status and gate
  requirement, every validation evidence state, the precedence of a step's own
  ticket, and the worst-prerequisite rule with all reasons listed. It walks a diamond
  from blocked through provisional to confirmed and finished, finds two- and
  three-step cycles across target projects with their downstream steps, shows the
  answer is the same in any step order, merges two accounts of one ticket (newer
  read, late outage, tie), and proves through the real gate registry that a
  superseded green gate stops counting. The plan registry is walked through
  idempotent, revised, conflicting and invalid definitions, per-owner capacity,
  older, repeated and unnamed observations, published levels that repeat, interleave,
  reverse and start again after the plan was emptied and refilled, and damaged or
  newer files that are never overwritten.
- `tests/readiness.rs` drives the shared runtime against real git stores: canonical
  ids and audit entries of `define`; a refused dispatch that claims nothing; an
  unplanned ticket that is not gated; levels following a run's dispatch and the
  target finishing its ticket; the override request, a refused AI answer, the
  person's approval used once, the note and audit trail, and a denial; a scripted CI
  adapter moving a step through pending, failed, passed, superseded and a pinned
  commit; a revoked grant making every reading stale and a refresh restoring it; a
  deleted prerequisite ticket; validation evidence from a real profile run; and the
  routes with their status codes.
- `remote_servers/readiness.rs` uses the owned CLI process to plan, be refused, ask
  for and receive an override, and read the levels from the event stream, then
  serves the routes from a real server behind its bearer and repeats the reads, a
  refused and an admitted dispatch through the stdio MCP tool.
- `contracts.spec.ts # HS2-42TARA` validates the real server's plan, readiness,
  ready-work, refusal, approval and event responses against the contract.
- Not verified here: dispatch at the provisional level, which is the next section
  (HS2-JSF985); a deployment gate from a real adapter, since none ships
  (HS2-G3VAK4).

### Orchestration provisional work across targets (HS2-JSF985)

- `provisional_tests.rs` (core) is a table over who allows speculation: the allowed
  case with its base, and one change at a time for the orchestration policy, each
  target override, each target's own setting (off and unknown), the opt-out tag on
  either ticket (set and never read), a deployment requirement and gates about two
  commits. It walks gate state by ticket state to show that only the provisional
  level gets an answer, counts depth through a three-project chain while each limit
  is raised and lowered and the deepest gate goes green and red again, ends a cycle
  without confirming it, and checks the same plan in another order. For the
  scheduler it pins the schedule without the opt-in against the same input with the
  rule's answer present, the wire shape without new members and the old tie order;
  then confirmed before provisional on a tie, the risk weight at 0, 50 and 100,
  caps counting a provisional start, a refill, and refused or undecided items never
  placed. The document store is created only by a change, keeps owners apart, is
  private, and never overwrites damaged or newer data.
- `tests/provisional.rs` (runtime) uses two bound targets with separate projects and
  ticket stores, a scripted CI adapter, a counting capacity probe and the
  `RecordingSessions` executor. Target 2's ticket B requires target 1's ticket A
  with CI. It covers: no policy and a policy without the opt-in giving the old
  refusal, schedule, outputs and no file; pending then green with the record, the
  events, the note, `run status`, `show` and `explain`, and a repeated dispatch;
  red with one note naming the run, the repair's urgency score and
  `provisional_dependents`, then a fix as a new run and as a newer commit on the
  same run, a fix that fails once, and work already integrated; a target that
  disallows speculation in six ways with nothing dispatched, started or recorded,
  and its later opt-in; a plan defined before the opt-in, whose tags are read by
  the first dispatch or scheduling pass; the depth limit over two and three layers
  with limits raised; a result written to the gate registry while nothing ran, applied once by
  reconciliation and once by a scheduling pass, an older result arriving late, and
  an owed note written once; scheduler starts only under `placement.automatic`,
  with confirmed work first under a cap of one; the `provisional_dispatch` approval
  for a dispatch and for a start, with a denial; an idle follower that runs no pass,
  contacts no target and rewrites nothing while the gate pends; reopen with its
  errors, audit and a later green result; a lost, re-watched and superseded gate;
  and the routes.
- `remote_servers/provisional.rs` serves two targets from a real server: the old
  refusal with no policy, the typed refusal while the projects have not opted in,
  the dispatch once they have, a red watch Job awaited on the event stream by
  cursor with exactly one note, the stdio MCP tool reading the ledger, `run status`
  and `explain` and reopening, and the owned CLI process reading and repeating it.
- `contracts.spec.ts # HS2-JSF985` validates the real server's speculation status,
  step readiness, run status, explanation, capacity snapshot, event page and reopen
  responses against the contract.
- Not verified: a session of a real AI tool started for provisional work (tests use
  the recording executor); a target on another machine reporting its own setting
  over the remote transport, which shares the capacity read covered by HS2-J8PRTV;
  acting on at-risk or reopened work, which is not built (HS2-2K0DM8); the workspace
  view (HS2-0D60T8).

  state with a pending cancel, an outage and a pause, the correction matrix, repeated

- `run_tests.rs # hs2_ezv83c` pins the run operation lock: it excludes another

### Orchestration CI and deployment gates (HS2-5JBYPV)

- `gate_tests.rs` (core) pins all 36 state edges, a 25-row table of what a provider
  reading does in each state, the coverage rule for both verdicts, late, duplicate
  and interleaved readings (asserting the stored file is byte-identical when nothing
  applies), idempotent links, supersession across commits and back, deployment
  approval edges, the rollup of every pair of states, request validation, a damaged
  or newer file, bounded history and capacity.
- `tests/gates.rs` drives the runtime with a scripted adapter whose wait blocks on a
  condition variable: link, sync, events once per change, an
  adapter that cannot start, the repository rule, a sync and a follower woken by the
  change and idle without gates, and deployments (no passed gate, a remembered rule,
  a production deployment that asks every time, denial, withdrawal with a superseded CI gate, a
  policy that asks first, a scripted executor's typed result). One test uses the real
  GitHub Actions adapter over a Job store and judges the watch Job the way the
  monitor does.
- `tests/access.rs` pins that `authorize` reads again after losing a race to a
  concurrent resolve, and still denies a race that never ends.
- `remote_servers/gates.rs` runs one runtime through authenticated HTTP, the stdio
  MCP tool on a live service and the owned CLI process: a subscriber of the run
  event stream sees the gate pass from the Job store's change with nobody calling
  sync, then a production deployment is requested, approved by a person and recorded.
- `tests/job_monitor.rs` (HS2-VVHVF0) runs the runtime with a stand-in monitor that
  holds the real monitor slot: a link starts it once and only for a waiting gate, a
  repeat finds it, a stopped one is started again, a settled gate starts none, a
  failed start leaves the link standing; a follower restarts a monitor that died,
  backs off a failing start (30 s, then 60 s) without launching between, and starts
  nothing without a grant; a sync makes sure of it before waiting.
- `remote_servers/job_monitor.rs` (HS2-VVHVF0) links a gate over HTTP and a real
  monitor process the server started watches it to green against a loopback
  provider with no CLI call. Then the run is cancelled and the monitor stopped, and
  a server built over the same home starts it again from its own start-up and
  records the next verdict. Disabling the start-up path fails the test.

  `hotsheet-jobs`), and deployment execution, which does not exist yet (HS2-G3VAK4).

### Machine capabilities and step requirements (HS2-ZY4Z4G)

- `capabilities_tests.rs` (core) matches every requirement kind (`os`, `arch`, `tools`,
  `toolchains`, `min_memory_gb` with its tolerance boundary, `gpu` any or by vendor)
  in each state (met, unmet, unknown), several misses in their fixed order, an older
  peer's snapshot without capabilities, the canonical form and every malformed value,
  the JSON wire form both ways, the capacity version with and without capabilities,
  and the owner's declared toolchains in the admission file.
- `scheduler_tests.rs # hs2_zy4z4g` packs work with requirements: unmet and unknown
  requirements never take a free session, the detail names the requirement, an
  unread machine is `capacity_not_read`, and the same work starts once the machine
  reports what it needs (empty, then refilled, then changed).
- `site_scheduling_tests.rs # hs2_9fktb3` (core, HS2-9FKTB3) places steps of a
  project with mixed-OS sites: the qualifying site wins and every other site is named
  with its reason; an offline site and one that did not report are `requirement_unknown`
  until one qualifies, then unmet again when it changes; steps of one project spread
  over machines under the machine cap and wait with each site's reason once all are
  full; a free session on another site is used before any start; ties go to the named
  site, then the lowest id, in any input order; a site removed between passes is not
  tried, one out of the policy is `policy_denied`, and one added back is used again;
  resources and refusal backoff are judged per site's machine; decision records keep
  the sites as codes.
- `site_scheduling_tests.rs # hs2_6nqkp9` (core, HS2-6NQKP9) gives two sites of one
  project different policy resources: each site is judged only by its own entry (held
  on the named site sends the work to the other; the named site's resource held on
  the other machine means nothing there; both held names each site's own), a site
  without an entry needs only the step's own resource, and two competing steps each
  take one site's resource.
- `tests/session_executor.rs # hs2_6nqkp9` runs the same through the runtime: with
  the named site's resource held, the dry run, `explain` (`declared_by: target`) and
  the applied start use the other site and its own resource, and the session's prompt
  names only that one.
- `remote_servers/e2e_sites.rs # hs2_6nqkp9` proves it across two servers: the home's
  resource held on the home's claim backend passes the home over by name, and the
  peer's session is told to acquire the peer's own resource. Its `converge` helper
  repeats a machine's sync pass at once, at most five times, while the pass reports
  `PushRaced` (HS2-457FGS). Since HS2-R2BC3N the pass retries a raced push itself.
- `tests/session_executor.rs # hs2_9fktb3` groups two bound targets as sites and
  limits the named one's machine: the dry-run plan and `explain` choose the other site
  and name why, the applied pass dispatches the step's run there and logs the sites,
  and after a refused start the orphaned run stays on its site and is started there.
- `tests/scheduler.rs # hs2_zy4z4g` defines a step with requirements through the
  runtime (aliases normalized), then `explain` and the applied pass move from
  `requirement_unknown` through `requirement_unmet` to a start as the probe changes.
- `host_health/capabilities_tests.rs` covers the pure parsers on every host (version

toolchains` changes what it reports. The dispatch and MCP tests pin `--require` and

  route, one refused, at 1440, 1100 and 390 and back, in Chromium and WebKit, and checks
  each ticket was asked once across a new version.

### Ordered default AI tool fallback (HS2-RWA8V6)

Legacy scalar and canonical array storage, validation, provider-choice
preservation, and unavailable-primary selection are covered in
`crates/hotsheet-plugins/src/tests.rs`. The ordered setting reader is covered
in `crates/hotsheet-ticketing/src/sync_ai/tests.rs`; automatic grouping's
failed-primary/backup-success, unusable-reply fallback, and all-failed transitions are covered in
`crates/hotsheet-server/src/auto_group.rs`. The real server settings roundtrip
is in `crates/hotsheet-server/tests/http.rs`. Client parsing, provider-order
mapping, settings rendering, and the shipped parent interaction are covered in
`clients/web/src/server-response-parsers.test.ts`,
`clients/web/src/ai-provider-defaults.test.ts`,
`clients/web/src/components/ai-tool-settings.test.ts`, and
`clients/web/tests/providers.spec.ts`. The live quota case remains in
`docs/manual-test-plan.md` because a real subscription limit is not a
deterministic fixture. The browser case waits for both overlay rails to settle
before reviewing the backup controls at 760px in light and dark themes.

HS2-ZX9CKC extends ordered fallback to sync repair. The shared
`sync_ai::tests::hs2_zx9ckc_a_typed_limit_retries_one_backup_after_the_prior_session_ends`
checks durable sequential retry, ticket reuse, and stale completion rejection.
`crates/hotsheet-server/tests/sync_ai.rs` exercises unavailable-primary selection and a
later server pass after a typed limit; `crates/hotsheet-cli/tests/cli.rs` exercises the
same ordered selection and a later headless `sync` retry with synthetic conflicts.

### Project Settings resize transition (HS2-B67JCN)

`clients/web/tests/providers.spec.ts` verifies the real Project Settings
composition at 1280 → 760 → 390 → 1280, waits for the Workbench's overlay
panel content to finish sliding before checking the AI tools region, and
opens and closes the Settings Sidebar at 760. Chromium and WebKit captures
confirm the settled pane is readable; the original clipped capture was taken
while the rails were transitioning.

### Recreated hosted store watcher (HS2-R6FZ54)

`crates/hotsheet-server/src/watcher.rs` tests parent event filtering, re-arm index
reconciliation that removes old rows and adds replacement rows, and the native watcher
transition for both root and `tickets/` scopes on Unix and the production root
scope on Windows, where a watched child prevents moving the parent directory.
Reconciliation also asserts a client invalidation; a corrupt source-hash transition preserves the healthy index row
and still emits that invalidation. The index test exercises the same outcome for
both full and Git-delta reconciliation and requires a second unchanged pass to
stay quiet. The native case verifies that a later
external write is indexed after the store is recreated, and that each removal marks
freshness out of sync before the next registration. Windows and Linux platform CI
must exercise their own native backends before the ticket completes.
The Windows-only identity test pins stable handle-based directory IDs across rename and
recreation at the same path; the Windows cfg check compiles that platform implementation.
Startup-race tests replace the watched directory after initial registration and remove it
before child registration, then recreate it. Both transitions run under root and `tickets/`
scopes on Unix and root scope on Windows before the native watch becomes live.
The replacement test covers both sides of the post-registration identity sample and checks
that a subsequent external write reaches the rearmed index.
